title: metadata-protocol: fold the two overlay-write close predicates (`namedBaseCloseSubject`, `packagelessCloseSubject`) into one fix-can-be-taken predicate
body:
domain:server#5 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQKwKFCp1m6Pb6Q8c1

Source: the contract review of PR #29270 (#28905), record 6577747588, should-fix S6 (the dev's open question 3, answered A). #28904 has landed (#29258), which was the precondition.

`namedBaseCloseSubject` (`protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`, #28905) and `packagelessCloseSubject` (`protocol-packageless-overlay-migration.ts`, #28576) agree step for step on whether the pair fix can be taken: the pair id derives, `customizationPairEnsureRefusal` answers none, the base records a `manifest.version`, and the D2 gate admits the declared body. They differ only where intended: the named close reads no row and accepts a named package among several shippers, while the package-less close requires exactly one shipper and classifies the stored row.

Ask: one shared predicate for the common steps, with each close keeping its own intended difference. This is a refactor with no behaviour change: both closes' pins pass unchanged, and the sentence spelling (`closedOverlayWriteClauses`) is untouched. Serial with the S1 card (same module).
